text: Writing clean code is a skill that separates good programmers from great ones. The most important goal is to make your code readable, not just for the computer, but for other humans. This starts with clear naming conventions; a variable called `userAge` is far easier to understand than `x`. Instead of writing long, complex blocks, you should break your work into small, focused functions. Each function should do one simple thing. This approach greatly improves maintainability. When another developer (or your future self) returns to the project, they can quickly understand the logic and make changes without fear of breaking everything. Ultimately, clean code saves time and reduces frustration for everyone involved.
